items.title: NovaFarm seed round
items.context: NovaFarm is negotiating a 2 M€ seed round at an 8 M€ pre-money valuation. The company has 8 million existing shares at 1 € per share. The investor asks for ownership computed on the post-money valuation.

questions.prompt: Compute the post-money valuation and the investor's ownership.
How many new shares must be issued at 1 € per share?
Name a major risk if the seed is delayed and a bridge becomes necessary.

criteria.label: Runway and dilution risk
criteria.model_answer: The runway shortens and the bridge may dilute further or impose unfavourable terms.

items.model_answer: Post-money 10 M€, investor 20%, 2 million new shares. A delayed bridge shortens the runway and increases dilution.

items.title: Helio Series A
items.context: Helio raises 6 M€ at a 24 M€ pre-money valuation. The term sheet provides an option pool of 10% of post-money, included in the pre-money. No other dilution is expected.

questions.prompt: Compute the post-money valuation and the investor's ownership.
Compute the value of the option pool and the founders' ownership after the pool.
Explain who bears the dilution of the pool and why the pre-money convention matters.

criteria.label: Founders bear the pre-money pool
criteria.model_answer: A pool included in the pre-money is taken before the investor enters: the founders bear its dilution.

items.model_answer: Post-money 30 M€, investor 20%, pool 3 M€, founders 70%. The pre-money convention makes the founders bear the pool.

items.title: Orion cap table
items.context: Orion has 6 million founder shares, 1 million granted options and 3 million shares held by an existing investor, for 10 million fully diluted shares. A new 4 M€ round at a 20 M€ post-money valuation targets a pool of 12% of post-money.

questions.prompt: Compute the founders' and the existing investor's ownership on the current fully diluted basis.
What is the new investor's ownership in the new round?
What is the value of the 12% target pool?
In which order do you verify the cap table after the round?

criteria.label: Order: pool, new shares, total, percentages
criteria.model_answer: Set the pool, issue the new shares, recompute the fully diluted total, then check that the percentages sum to 100%.

items.model_answer: Founders 60%, existing investor 30%, new investor 20%, pool 2.4 M€. Verify the fully diluted total and the sum to 100%.

items.title: Apex waterfall
items.context: Apex is sold for 12 M€. Investor A invested 4 M€ with a 1x participating preference with no cap and holds 25% of the shares. Investor B invested 2 M€ with a 1x participating preference and holds 15%. The founders hold 60%. No debt or transaction costs.

questions.prompt: How much does investor A receive?

criteria.label: A receives 5.5 M€
criteria.model_answer: A receives 4 M€ preference + 25% x (12 - 4 - 2) = 4 + 1.5 = 5.5 M€.

questions.prompt: How much does investor B receive?

criteria.label: B receives 2.9 M€
criteria.model_answer: B receives 2 M€ preference + 15% x 6 = 2 + 0.9 = 2.9 M€.

questions.prompt: How much do the founders receive?
Explain the waterfall order and verify that the total distributed is 12 M€.

criteria.label: Preferences then residual, total 12 M€
criteria.model_answer: Pay preferences first (4 + 2 = 6 M€), then share the 6 M€ residual pro rata: A 1.5, B 0.9, founders 3.6. Total 12 M€.

items.model_answer: A 5.5 M€, B 2.9 M€, founders 3.6 M€. Total 12 M€. Preferences first, then residual pro rata.
